title: How reflexive hepatitis C testing helps close diagnostic gaps
summary: A study of 38 million tests found that clinician-ordered reflex hepatitis C testing improved follow-up RNA testing and reduced diagnostic delays.
body_markdown:
*Hepatitis C is curable, yet many people never complete the testing needed to confirm an active infection and begin treatment.*


New research from Labcorp, published in[Clinical Infectious Diseases](https://academic.oup.com/cid/advance-article-abstract/doi/10.1093/cid/ciag227/8643933) , suggests that a change in how hepatitis C testing is ordered may help close that gap and help more patients complete the testing needed for diagnosis. Researchers found that the widespread adoption of[reflexive hepatitis C testing](https://www.labcorp.com/treatment-areas/virology-infectious-diseases/clinical-testing/hepatitis/hepatitis-c) , which automatically performs an RNA test from the same sample after a positive antibody result, was associated with faster follow-up testing and improved identification of active infections.


## Why diagnosing hepatitis C can be challenging


Hepatitis C is a viral infection that causes liver inflammation. The CDC estimates that approximately[2.2 million](https://stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/154130/cdc_154130_DS1.pdf) U.S. adults are living with hepatitis C infection and nearly[one in three people](https://www.cdc.gov/hepatitis-c/hcp/diagnosis-testing/index.html) with hepatitis C are unaware of their infection status *.* Symptoms can go unnoticed for years, and if left untreated, the infection can lead to cirrhosis, liver failure, or other serious complications.


Diagnosing hepatitis C typically requires two steps:


- Step 1: An antibody test identifies prior exposure to the virus
- Step 2: An RNA test detects hepatitis C in the blood to confirm whether an active infection is present


Traditionally, a positive hepatitis C screening result required a clinician to order a second test to determine whether the infection was active. That extra step could create delays or prevent patients from completing the follow-up testing needed for diagnosis. Reflexive testing removes that hurdle by allowing clinicians to include follow-up RNA testing as part of the initial test order, enabling the second test to be performed automatically using the same sample, when needed.


## A major shift in hepatitis C testing practices


In recent years, expanded[national hepatitis C screening recommendations](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/wr/mm7228a2.htm) , clinician education efforts, and improvements to test-ordering tools helped support the shift to reflexive testing.


To evaluate these changes, researchers analyzed more than 38 million hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody tests and 1.4 million follow-up HCV RNA tests performed by Labcorp between 2018 and 2024. The findings document a shift in hepatitis C testing practices over the six-year study period.


Adoption of reflexive testing increased from about 22% of antibody-positive patients in 2018 to more than 82% in 2024. During that same period, follow-up RNA testing increased from 66% to nearly 89%, while same-day testing more than doubled.


The results suggest that eliminating extra steps in the testing process may help more patients receive the follow-up testing needed to confirm an active infection.


##


## Advancing hepatitis C detection and treatment


Hepatitis C is highly treatable, with modern antiviral therapies[treating more than 95% of infections](https://www.cdc.gov/hepatitis-c/hcp/clinical-care/index.html) , making timely diagnosis a critical first step.


“One of the biggest challenges in hepatitis C care isn't screening. It's making sure patients complete the follow-up testing needed to confirm an active infection," said Laura Gillim, Ph.D., medical science liaison and discipline director for infectious diseases at Labcorp.


"Our findings suggest that when that extra step is removed, more patients receive the testing they need, helping move them closer to diagnosis and treatment.”


By simplifying the process from initial screening to confirmatory testing, reflexive HCV testing can help more patients receive a timely diagnosis and reduce delays in connecting them to care.


**Read the study:** *Trends in Reflexive Hepatitis C Virus Testing in a National US Laboratory: A Retrospective Study From 2018 to 2024* , published in[Clinical Infectious Diseases](https://academic.oup.com/cid/advance-article-abstract/doi/10.1093/cid/ciag227/8643933) .


## About the Author


[Laura Gillim, Ph.D](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/bios/laura-gillim-phd) ***.,** is the medical science liaison and discipline director for infectious diseases at Labcorp, where she provides scientific leadership, expert clinical consultation, and strategic guidance across Labcorp’s infectious disease portfolio. She holds a B.S. in molecular and cellular biology from Haverford College and a Ph.D. in biomedical sciences from the Mount Sinai School of Medicine.
